DENAH (Digital Ecosystem & Navigation fo: DENAH (Digital Ecosystem & Navigation for Area Housing) is a geospatial data-based settlement mapping and classification platform. Its goal is to provide accurate spatial information for spatial planning, settlement area management, and data-driven decision-making.
DENAH (Digital Ecosystem & Navigation for Area Housing) is a WebGIS platform developed to present spatial information on the distribution of settlements in Bengkulu Province.
DENAH memanfaatkan hasil pengolahan citr: DENAH utilizes satellite imagery processing and Machine Learning-based classification methods to produce spatial settlement information. The classification results are then integrated into a database and visualized through a WebGIS, making them easier to explore.
DENAH mengintegrasikan data hasil klasif: DENAH integrates satellite imagery classification results from Google Earth Engine (GEE) into an interactive WebGIS system. Users can explore settlement distribution by administrative area and year, and view statistical information derived from the spatial data.
DENAH merupakan WebGIS yang menyajikan i: DENAH is a WebGIS that presents spatial information on the distribution of settlements in Bengkulu Province based on the processing and classification of satellite imagery. The mapping data covers the 2021–2025 period, making it possible to observe patterns and the development of settlements over time.

The classification results are further processed into spatial data that can be stored, managed, and displayed through the DENAH WebGIS system.

Hasil klasifikasi diperiksa secara visua: The classification results are reviewed visually by comparing them against satellite imagery and the spatial conditions of the study area to ensure the spatial patterns are appropriate and to reduce interpretation errors.
Hasil proses Random Forest berupa raster: The Random Forest process produces a classification raster that assigns a class value to each pixel. These results serve as the basis for identifying areas classified as settlements. The classification data is stored at a 10-meter spatial resolution.
Hasil raster klasifikasi dikonversi menj: The classification raster is converted into vector/polygon data so that classified areas can be managed as spatial data. The data is then exported in SHP and GeoJSON formats.

The model uses 100 decision trees and is trained on the training samples and all features in the composite imagery. The model then predicts the class for each pixel to produce a classification map.
